info.name: route-policy
info.description:
Route-policy service (ai/route-policy): rulesets of evaluators pick the LiteLLM chain alias for each `auto` turn, and every decision is logged to route-policy-db (Trino: postgres_route_policy). Phase 3: the `default` ruleset ENFORCES -- LiteLLM's pre-call hook awaits POST /decide for every `auto` request (within ROUTE_POLICY_DECIDE_TIMEOUT_S, 0.25 s) and serves the chain it returns in the same pass; a timeout, an error or `apply: false` sends the turn to local-private. Called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/route-policy` → `http://route-policy:8000`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET/POST, `forward_headers: true`, `auth: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key: set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` — every request inherits them via collection-level auth.

Direct base URL (bypassing LiteLLM): http://route-policy:8000 inside ai_shared (what LiteLLM's hook uses), or http://<host>:${PORT_ROUTE_POLICY} (default 8027), which the ai/edge HAProxy publishes for clients in EDGE_ALLOWED_CIDRS — no auth there. Drop `/v1/route-policy` from the paths when you use it.

Workflow: GET /evaluator-types (what a ruleset may contain) → GET /rulesets/:rulesetId (the live `default`) → POST /evaluate (dry-run on a conversation) → POST /decide + POST /observe with the same `decisionId` (what the hook sends) → GET /chats/:chatId/decisions. See ai/route-policy/ROUTE_POLICY.md for the full reference.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://api.zeoenergy.com.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). The pass-through runs with `auth: true`, so a non-admin virtual key needs `/v1/route-policy` in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` — set under `metadata`, by a proxy admin, because the top-level field is Enterprise-only; the master key works without it. Otherwise 403. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

A UUID shared by POST /decide and POST /observe (the hook makes a fresh uuid4 per request). Re-sending /decide with the same value replays the FIRST stored decision; set a new one (e.g. Postman's {{$guid}}) for a new decision.
Chat id sent as `chat_id` on POST /decide, and read back by GET /chats/:chatId/decisions (fill that request's path variable with it).

request.description: Liveness, and what the compose healthcheck and the edge probe. Returns {status: "ok", rulesets: [{id, version}, ...] (the compiled versions this copy has cached), bindings: <count>}. A running process has finished startup, which required route-policy-db (migrations + ruleset seeding); /health itself does not touch the database. See ROUTE_POLICY.md § API.

Readiness: a live SELECT 1 on route-policy-db. 200 {status: "ready", db: "up"} when decisions can be logged right now; 503 {status: "not ready", db: "down"} otherwise (the service still DECIDES from its cached rulesets then; only logging stops).

Prometheus text: route_policy_decisions_total{route,mode,applied}, route_policy_decide_seconds, route_policy_evaluator_seconds{evaluator,type}, route_policy_votes_total{evaluator,type,outcome}, route_policy_invariant_overrides_total{invariant}, route_policy_observations_total{status}, route_policy_duplicates_total{endpoint}, route_policy_errors_total{kind}, plus the HTTP metrics of prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator. Scraped by the litellm stack's prometheus (job route-policy). See ROUTE_POLICY.md § Metrics.

What a ruleset can contain. evaluator_types: every registered type (regex_text, tool_calls, cooldown, backend_load, static) with its config JSON schema and DECLARED output (summary, when it votes, what one exchange's relevance means -- null when it cannot judge single exchanges -- and every detail key with its kind). combiner_types: priority, weighted with their option schemas. roles: vote | force | veto. The declarations live next to each evaluator and are tested against the real code. See ROUTE_POLICY.md § Evaluators.

Decide (and log) the chain alias for one request -- what LiteLLM's pre-call hook sends on every `auto` request, and AWAITS (ROUTE_POLICY_DECIDE_TIMEOUT_S, 0.25 s): it rewrites `auto` to `route` when `apply` is true and its own copy of the invariants agrees, else to local-private. The bound ruleset (bindings: auto -> default) runs every evaluator, its combiner picks one route, and the invariants have the last word (requested local-private stays local-private; the route is always one of the ruleset's chain aliases).

Body (the contract, ROUTE_POLICY_PLAN § 7): decision_id (a UUID the caller makes), requested_model, litellm_call_id, chat_id, message_id, user_id, key_alias (all nullable), messages (OpenAI messages as LiteLLM received them), tools (or null), backends ({api_base: {verdict: ok|busy|down|stale|unknown, waiting, running}}). Unknown fields are ignored.

200: {decision_id, route, mode, apply, ruleset: {id, version}, votes: [{evaluator, type, route, weight, confidence, role, abstained, reason, latency_ms}], scores, latency_ms}. apply is true only for an enforce ruleset whose invariants held -- the `default` ruleset (version 2) is enforce, so this example answers apply: true. This example routes to local-code through `sticky-code` (a sandbox tool was called one exchange ago).

Idempotent: a repeated decision_id returns the FIRST stored decision, whatever the new body says. 404: no ruleset bound to requested_model. 422: decision_id not a UUID, wrong types. 503: the bound ruleset cannot be compiled by this copy. A decision is returned even when route-policy-db is down (it is then not logged), and in time: the decision write is waited for at most ROUTE_POLICY_DECISION_WRITE_BUDGET_S (0.05 s), then finishes in the background. See ROUTE_POLICY.md § API.

Record what really answered a decided request -- what the hook sends after the call, with the same decision_id. May arrive before or after /decide (no foreign key; the decision_outcomes view joins them). Body: decision_id, litellm_call_id, response_id (the provider's chatcmpl-..., what LiteLLM_SpendLogs.request_id holds), served_model_group (the chain), served_deployment, overflow_reason (busy | down | null), finish_reason, tool_calls (names), status (success | failure), error.

202: {decision_id, stored: true}; stored: false when this decision_id already had an outcome (the first write wins); {decision_id, stored: null, deferred: true} when the write outlasted ROUTE_POLICY_DECISION_WRITE_BUDGET_S and goes on in the background. 422: decision_id not a UUID. 503: the outcome could not be stored (no database, the write failed in time, or too many writes in flight). See ROUTE_POLICY.md § API.

Dry-run a stored ruleset version (version omitted = the highest; on the box `default` 1, the phase-2 shadow version, is still stored and evaluable) on a conversation. Writes nothing. Returns the /decide shape with decision_id: null and, per vote, the evaluator's `detail` (its declared output, GET /evaluator-types) and `error`. requested_model defaults to auto; send local-private to see the privacy invariant. 404: no such version. 422: give exactly one of `ruleset` / `document`. See ROUTE_POLICY.md § API.

Dry-run an UNSAVED ruleset document -- how a new version is tried before it is seeded. patterns_ref refs resolve inside the baked rulesets directory (a path that leaves it is a 422); a document copied from GET /rulesets/:rulesetId/:rulesetVersion posts back as is. Here a weighted, load-aware draft sends a general question to local-reasoning while qwen3.8-solo is busy. 422 with detail.errors listing EVERY problem when the document is invalid. Writes nothing. See ROUTE_POLICY.md § Rulesets.

Every stored ruleset version, without documents: {rulesets: [{id, version, mode, description, sha256, source, created_at, created_by, active_from, active_to}]}. active_from = first time a binding pointed at it; active_to = when none does any more (null while bound). 503 when route-policy-db is unavailable.
The highest version of one ruleset with its resolved document (refs inlined, exactly as hashed), plus `versions`: every version's summary. 404: no such ruleset.

One version with its document. Versions are immutable: changed content is a new version (a seed whose content differs from the stored version stops the service at startup). 404: no such version; 422: version < 1.

Which ruleset decides for which requested model: {bindings: [{scope_model, scope_key_alias (null = every key), ruleset_id, version, updated_at, updated_by}]}. Startup seeds auto -> default @ the highest baked-in version (rulesets/bindings.yaml); editing bindings is the phase-5 write API. The binding decides every `auto` turn.

variable.description: Open WebUI chat id (the X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id header LiteLLM forwards as chat_id).

request.description: One conversation's latest `limit` decisions, OLDEST FIRST, each with its votes and its outcome (null until /observe arrives; `agree` = the decided route equals the chain that served). An unknown chat id is an empty list. 503 when route-policy-db is unavailable.
